unit: Does trap #117's prescribed remedy (a single EXTERNAL launch anchor) actually catch the second of the two defects that founded the trap?

target_of_attack.claim: internal-consistency checks are blind by construction and 'the only defence is an external anchor -- a published certified value asserted before any swept configuration runs'; remedy as worded takes ONE published certified number, the launch lam_min
target_of_attack.owner: machine1, trap register #117 (0692b52) and m1-L160 sect2 (414c550), founded 2026-09-05
target_of_attack.why_now: my cycle-27 S3/D4 runner is itself a port of the cycle-25 S2 machinery, i.e. exactly the #117 fingerprint; I have to adopt the remedy this cycle and I am not adopting a remedy I have not fired at

not_a_12h_reveal_object: This leg attacks a claim published 2026-09-05 by m1; it is not a scored prediction about an unmeasured site. The 12h reveal gap is honoured for the S3/D4 prereg (leg A), which is pushed UNRUN.
control: variant 'clean' must reproduce ANCHOR-U 1.1761206927485314567e-5, ANCHOR-0 2.0004746865698620975e-5 and ANCHOR-D 1.9160562986370759475e-5 to the printed digits. If it does not, the whole run is VOID and nothing below is graded.

hypotheses.kind: EMPTY BY ALGEBRA -- declared before running, a DEMONSTRATION, not a test
hypotheses.claim: variant c1's composed launch lam_min equals clean's to all 40 dps (relative diff < 1e-35).
hypotheses.why_empty: at delta=0, p == q so up == uq elementwise; the corrupt and clean summands coincide term by term. No measurement in any world can fire this. Stated as such per trap #116, which I founded.
hypotheses.grade_role: control on the transplant being faithful, NOT evidence

hypotheses.kind: REAL TEST, magnitude genuinely unknown before the run
hypotheses.claim: variant c1's R2 lam_min differs from clean's by relative error > 1e-3, i.e. the defect the launch anchor cannot see is NOT numerically harmless at a graded configuration.
hypotheses.fires_against_me_if: rel err <= 1e-6 (then #117's blind spot is inconsequential and my attack is a nitpick)

hypotheses.kind: REAL TEST of m1's own structural claim (I expect it to SUPPORT him)
hypotheses.claim: the internal checks I1 (trace identity) and I3 (G-orthonormality) are <= 1e-25 on BOTH corrupt variants, i.e. as clean as on the clean instrument.
hypotheses.fires_against_me_if: either corrupt variant degrades I1 or I3 by more than 1e6x relative to clean -- which would mean internal checks are NOT blind and #117 overstates

hypotheses.kind: REAL TEST, firing set non-empty BY MEASUREMENT
hypotheses.claim: variant c2's composed launch lam_min differs from ANCHOR-0 by relative error > 1e-3, i.e. the prescribed anchor DOES fire on the first defect class.
hypotheses.fires_against_me_if: rel err <= 1e-3 (then the anchor is blind to BOTH classes and my framing 'proper subset' is wrong -- it would be a stronger negative than the one I am claiming)

hypotheses.kind: NOT INDEPENDENT OF HB -- declared. Same underlying quantity (c1's error at d != 0), different rung.
hypotheses.claim: variant c1's R0 lam_min differs from ANCHOR-D 1.9160562986370759475e-5 by relative error > 1e-6, i.e. a certified DISPLACED anchor catches what the launch anchor cannot.
hypotheses.why_declared_dependent: my own standing law: two determinations descending from one approximation are one determination twice. HE is the constructive half (a remedy exists and is already published) of the same fact HB measures; it is not corroboration of HB.

what_would_make_this_leg_worthless: if clean fails the control; or if HB fires against me (harmless corruption); or if HD fires against me in the direction that makes the anchor blind to everything, in which case the finding is different and larger and I must say so.
